title: Parvin E'tesami's birth chart
metaDescription: Parvin E'tesami's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 24.6° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Mars holds a opposition to Pluto at 0.0° — close enough to weld drive to depth. An opposition puts two needs on opposite shores of the same water. Neither drowns; neither gets the whole beach.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 24.6° of Pisces is the Sun's exact seat — third decan, 20°–30°, sub-ruled by Mars in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 28.3° Pisces; Venus stands at 10.7° Aquarius; Mars stands at 21.7° Sagittarius. The tradition reads thought steeped in tone and memory from Mercury, attraction that begins as conversation from Venus, effort spent in bursts and openings from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mars to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a opposition within 0.0°. The scheme reads an opposition as a axis to walk, not a fight to win: the chart keeps both ends lit. Behind it, Uranus opposition Neptune at 2.4°, and the Sun square Pluto at 2.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mars opposes Pluto while both square the Sun. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. Venus makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags two placements in this chart. Mercury in Pisces at 28.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Cancer at 1.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: water 5, fire 2, air 2, earth 1 across the elements, and mutable 5, cardinal 4, fixed 1 across the modalities. Mercury and Neptune were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aries for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.0° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 20.6°.
